community.description: An observational report describes midday siestas among adults in Spain, with regular nappers often reporting four days a week.

source.title: Researchers study how daytime naps may influence health - NHLBI

catalog:recovery:nap.notes: The original Sleep Foundation page returned HTTP 403 through both retrieval methods. The replacement describes observed siestas, not a recommended nap duration or an intervention.

checks.reason: Direct retrieval and the web-fetch tool both returned HTTP 403; no claim was retained from this inaccessible page.
The live NIH report explicitly describes observed regular midday siestas in a Spanish adult cohort, often four days a week. Its health-outcome associations are not repeated.

community.description: NCCIH describes ashwagandha as a medicinal plant historically used in traditional Ayurvedic practice.

catalog:supplement:ashwagandha.notes: The independently retrieved full NIH page contains a traditional-use report, not just navigation. Like the berberine description, this records a historical medicinal tradition without repeating indications, recommendations or claimed benefits.

checks.reason: The background section explicitly records longstanding medicinal-plant use, especially in Ayurvedic medicine. Current promotional indications and trial results were not repurposed.

community.description: NCCIH describes fenugreek seeds historically used as a culinary spice and in traditional medicine.

catalog:supplement:fenugreek.notes: The full public NIH page was independently retrieved and inspected. It reports historical culinary and medicinal use of the seeds; promoted indications, safety assertions and clinical results were not imported.

checks.reason: The background section explicitly records seeds used as a spice and traditional medicine. The description does not turn the page's promoted uses into verified benefits.

community.description: An exercise-nutrition guide describes regular caffeine intake through coffee, energy drinks and caffeinated soft drinks, alongside caffeine anhydrous supplements.

source.title: How Caffeine Improves Exercise Performance - Healthline

catalog:supplement:caffeine.notes: The original numerical amounts were presented by the page as recommendations and study-based amounts. The revised description retains explicit consumption forms without implying an observed common dose.

checks.reason: The live page names regular intake through coffee, energy drinks and caffeinated soda, and separately discusses caffeine anhydrous supplements. Dose and efficacy recommendations were excluded.
